walkthroughs.body_html:
Unit 1: The Study of Prose — a core area of GCSE English Literature.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Unit 1: The Study of Prose brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Unit 1: The Study of Prose.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: How many witches appear in Macbeth?

options: Verbal irony is when you make a joke about something.
Verbal irony is just saying something unexpected.
Enjambment is when a poem uses no punctuation at all.
When a speaker says one thing but means another — typically the opposite — relying on shared context for the listener to detect the gap.

mcqs.q: What is the function of dystopian fiction?
options: Enjambment is when a poem uses no punctuation at all.
Dystopian fiction predicts what will actually happen in 100 years.
Dystopian fiction is just storytelling set in scary futures.
To critique tendencies in the writer's own society by extrapolating them into a nightmarish future — dystopias hold up a warning mirror to the present.
Verbal irony is when you make a joke about something.
When a sentence or phrase runs over from one line of poetry to the next without a punctuated pause, creating flow or surprise across the line break.
Enjambment is when a poem uses no punctuation at all.
Enjambment is when a poem has very long lines.
